name: Esteros del Iberá
story: Esteros del Iberá is a mix of swamps, bogs, stagnant lakes, lagoons, natural slough, and courses of water in the province of Corrientes, Argentina. It is one of the most important freshwater reservoirs in South America and the second-largest wetland in the world after Pantanal in Brazil. It is home to a wide variety of fauna, including capybara, caimans, snakes, frogs, anteaters, otters, deer, and many species of birds.
matters: The park is a stronghold of the vulnerable species marsh deer and strange-tailed tyrant and contains large populations of capybara, yacare caiman and broad-snouted caiman. It protects a portion of the Iberá Wetlands, one of the largest wetlands in the world.
